_comment: The only per-repo file in this skill. SKILL.md and repos.md are identical
across every repo that uses /ai-dev — when you copy the skill to another
project, edit this file and nothing else.
'toolkit' is the shared UI library this repo consumes from sources via a
relative path. Set it to null in a repo that has no such dependency.
runInstructions: Lunamux is a desktop/mobile app, not a web app — how you verify depends on what
you changed, and several targets cannot be driven headlessly at all. Be honest in
the PR about which of these you actually ran.
Server only:
./gradlew :server:run -Dlunamux.port={port} -Dlunamux.dbPath=/tmp/ai-dev/{key}.db
:server:run blocks until interrupted — background it (run_in_background, or `… &`)
and poll the port until it answers. In the foreground it hangs you until you time
out, with nothing verified. The same goes for the Electron scripts below.
Both flags are isolation, not decoration. The default debug port is 8444 and the
default dev database is shared, so two tickets running at once would contend on
the same port and race on the same SQLite file and its WAL. Never point a run at
the production database (termtastic.db) or the production port (8443).
Electron desktop shell: scripts/run-electron-dev.sh starts its own server and
reuses one already listening on the dev port — which is exactly the collision the
flags above avoid, so do NOT run it while another ticket may be building. Prefer
scripts/run-electron-demo.sh, which uses an in-process fake server and touches no
shared port or database. Both open a window: they need a desktop session and
cannot run headless.
Android and iOS cannot be verified in this automation. Do not try to boot an
emulator or simulator. State the gap in the PR's Verification section instead.
Web target: ./gradlew :web:jsBrowserDevelopmentExecutableDistribution builds the
bundle, and scripts/build-demo-web.sh produces the demo build.
Kill anything you started — scripts/kill-dev-server.sh. Never touch
scripts/kill-prod-server.sh.
